A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, methods, and research questions. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison after accounting for relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original feature-description evaluations, method ablations, qualitative analysis, and experiments reviving dead SAE features.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds human evaluations and a steering-sensitivity experiment.

M1.justification: VocabProj, TokenChange, and the raw-data and concatenation ensembles retain their procedures in Section 4 and Appendix B. The changed evaluation judge does not alter the description-generation methods.

E1.justification: The feature-description tasks, source datasets, and model families remain covered. New human and steering evaluations reuse this coverage. GPT-2 sample counts and SAE widths are setting changes; additional Gemma sizes appear in compute estimates.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain MaxAct, MaxAct++ for Llama-3.1 Instruct, and the same output-centric and ensemble methods. The Neuronpedia comparison also remains. New human and cost analyses compare existing methods.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported output judge from Gemini 1.5 Pro to GPT-4o mini and the GPT-2 feature count from 1,440 to 2,880. V2 Table 7 specifies 32K GPT-2 SAEs, replacing v1 Table 6's averaging across widths. Human-rating and higher-KL evaluation protocols are added. These reported changes do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds human validation of the LLM judge and direct human ratings of description faithfulness in Appendix E, a higher-clamping sensitivity check on 800 Gemma-2 features in Appendix A, and computational-cost analysis in Appendix D. These substantially expand validation beyond v1's retained ablations and qualitative analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix E.1 introduces the alternative annotator statistical test, specifying epsilon = 0.15 and reporting p = 0.03. Existing 95% confidence intervals and the 9,999-resample bootstrap procedure remain; no increased repeated-run or seed count is established.

E6.justification: V2 adds human-rating distributions, judge-validation results, FLOP estimates, and steering-sensitivity findings. GPT-2 results change in Table 7 and Figure 10: for example, MaxAct MLP input/output scores change from 41.3/32.6 to 39.7/34.0 under revised reported settings, so these are not same-setting performance changes. Main Table 1 and the dead-feature findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The feature definitions, invertible-featurizer framework, projection equation, and mathematical evaluation criteria remain unchanged. The added FLOP heuristic supports cost estimation rather than introducing a new theoretical derivation or formal result.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a potential-benefit claim for model editing, machine unlearning, and circuit analysis. The abstract and principal contributions retain their claims about complementary input/output descriptions, efficiency, ensembles, and reviving dead features.

C2.justification: V2 newly acknowledges that binary input evaluation can oversimplify feature behavior and that promoted versus suppressed concepts are not distinguished. Appendix E discusses human-rating difficulty and possible bias favoring MaxAct through reused activation data; Appendix A explains why stronger steering can produce unrepresentative, degenerate text.

D1.justification: V2 provides human-annotation instructions and study details, documents FLOP-estimation assumptions, and discloses ChatGPT assistance with helper functions. Existing method prompts, hardware, packages, and code-access information remain; the original clamping settings are relocated rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: V2 adds Calderon et al. for judge validation, Kaplan et al. and Anil et al. for compute estimation, and Wu et al. for model editing, while removing Elhage et al. (2022). Overall positioning remains stable. Added Farrell and Marks bibliography entries correspond to works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. V2 makes local wording corrections, expands explanations and limitations, adds computational-cost and human-evaluation appendix sections, and moves clamping details into Appendix A.

P2.justification: V2 adds the FLOP table and human-rating, annotation-instruction, and degeneration figures. It restructures the supplementary GPT-2 table and updates GPT-2 plots, including an axis scale. Existing visuals largely retain their design despite relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: Human validation, steering sensitivity, quantified compute estimates, and clearer limitations provide useful additional support for the existing conclusions. However, the reported output-judge change is not reconciled with the unchanged main results in Table 1. The revision improves confidence and transparency while leaving this evaluation-reporting ambiguity.
